papers.title: Bridging the implementation gap: a qualitative study of barriers to integrating psychological care into rheumatoid arthritis services in Iran.
papers.abstract: Despite robust evidence and explicit guideline recommendations, psychological care is rarely integrated into routine Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA) services in Iran. This study explored the multilevel barriers to this implementation gap. A qualitative study guided by the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) was conducted. Semi-structured interviews were held with 34 stakeholders (12 patients, 8 rheumatologists, 7 nurses, 4 psychologists, 3 hospital managers) in Iranian rheumatology clinics. Data were analyzed using directed content analysis. Barriers interacted across CFIR domains, forming an interpretive model of a reinforcing cycle. Financial exclusion (Outer Setting) reinforced biomedical clinic culture (Inner Setting), which diminished professional self-efficacy (Characteristics of Individuals) and nullified implementation processes. Stigma and lack of structured pathways were key themes. The integration gap reflects systemic misalignment, not a lack of evidence. Closing it requires coordinated policy, organizational, and educational reforms, not isolated interventions.
papers.summary: 本研究採用實施研究綜合框架（CFIR），透過訪談伊朗34名類風濕性關節炎（RA）領域的利益相關者，探討心理護理未能整合至常規RA服務中的多層級障礙。研究發現，財務排斥、生物醫學導向的診所文化、專業自我效能感低落以及病識感污名化等因素相互作用，形成惡性循環，導致實施過程失效，且缺乏結構化的轉介路徑亦為關鍵問題。
papers.significance: 該研究揭示了伊朗類風濕性關節炎醫療中「實施差距」的深層系統性原因，強調此問題並非源於缺乏臨床證據，而是系統性的資源與文化錯位。這對醫療政策制定者具有重要啟示：單一的干預措施無法解決問題，必須透過協調一致的醫療政策、組織變革與教育改革，才能有效將心理護理納入常規醫療體系，提升整體照護品質。
